description:
Plas Gogerddan is a long-lived funerary site, with a Bronze Age standing stone, round barrows, Iron Age cremation deposits, enclosures, and finally an Early Medieval cemetery. Our point of interest is a 7m x 5m rectangular timber structure enclosing a single central grave, which Ken Murphy has suggested may be an early church, possibly linked to the contemporary St. Padarn.

I am skeptical of interpreting this structure as a church, or kind of early chapel. It might be better understood as a kind of funerary shrine, the stone-lined pit could plausibly have been for votive deposits or libations associated with the dead. No material was recovered from within the pit so this is speculation on my part.
